After earlier this year launching parental managed accounts for preschool children, WhatsApp today expanded its parental supervision features to teen accounts, adding group activity alerts and additional restrictions on Meta AI. Details below.

WhatsApp expands parental supervision options

Earlier this year, WhatsApp announced a series of new features designed to give parents greater control over their preschool children's accounts.

These include letting parents decide who can contact the account and which groups the account can join, as well as the ability to view message requests from unknown contacts and manage the account's privacy settings, with all related changes protected by a parent-set PIN code.

A few weeks ago, WhatsApp further expanded this feature on iOS by adding a dedicated "Parental Supervision" section in the Settings app, making it easier for parents to find and configure managed accounts.

WhatsApp today expanded these supervision features once again, this time extending parental supervision to teenagers rather than being limited to preschool children, while also giving parents greater visibility into their children's group activity and more say in how they interact with channels, status updates, and most importantly, Meta AI.

After the update, parents will receive notifications when their teen's account joins or leaves a group, as well as when the membership of a group they have already joined "significantly increases." Parents can now also choose how their children use channels, whose status updates are visible to them, and who can see their children's status updates.

As for Meta AI, parents can now choose between the standard experience designed for users aged 13 and above, and a stricter "limited content" option, depending on which they feel is more appropriate for their children.

WhatsApp said the "limited content" setting further restricts the topics teenagers can discuss with Meta AI. When this setting is enabled, Meta AI features that rely on "Private Processing" will also become unavailable.

WhatsApp reiterated that these parental supervision features will not allow parents to view the actual messages or call content of their children, as such communications remain protected by end-to-end encryption.
